# SdkWork Claw Router v0.2.0

Release date: 2026-05-16

## Scope

This release record covers the capability slice developed after the successful `v0.1.0` release. The main change is configurable Claw Router authentication runtime behavior across the admin API, app API, portal runtime, OpenAPI contracts, and generated SDKs.

No separately published failed version exists after `v0.1.0`. During `v0.2.0` publication, an initial GitHub package workflow failed before build because checkout tried to hydrate Git LFS objects after the repository exceeded its LFS budget. That failed attempt is folded into this release record, and the final published release removes the runtime packaging dependency on LFS.

## Delivered

- Added admin-managed authentication settings for Claw Router, including login methods, QR login, OAuth visibility, recovery methods, registration methods, and verification policy flags.
- Added product-domain ports and SQL stores for admin auth settings, with SQLite and PostgreSQL implementations wired through the product infrastructure module registry.
- Added app runtime auth settings retrieval so the portal login experience can read the active tenant or organization policy instead of using a hard-coded auth method matrix.
- Added policy enforcement for password, email code, phone code, QR, session bridge, recovery, and registration verification flows.
- Preserved the stricter default auth posture: password login remains enabled by default while QR, code login, OAuth, and session bridge require explicit settings.
- Updated the portal auth routes to consume runtime auth config through the shared generated SDK surface rather than a static local configuration.
- Added an admin auth settings page and routing so operators can manage authentication UI and policy behavior from the portal.
- Updated OpenAPI outputs, API contract manifests, schema registries, frontend operation manifests, and generated TypeScript SDK types for the new auth settings endpoints and payloads.
- Adjusted app session and app auth tests so bridge, QR, code login, and registration verification cases explicitly opt into the runtime policy they are validating.
- Clarified installer CLI test setup so SQLite installer scenarios declare the desktop deployment profile explicitly.
- Added final platform-native release installers for service and desktop package modes: Linux `.deb` packages for Ubuntu/Debian `apt install`, Windows `.msi` packages through WiX, and macOS `.pkg` packages through `pkgbuild`.
- Updated GitHub release packaging so `archive` and `container` remain portable packages while `service` and `desktop` upload native installers instead of only `.tar.gz` or `.zip` archives.
- Changed server/service/container release package defaults to structured PostgreSQL runtime configuration, while desktop packages keep local SQLite by default.
- Updated Linux `.deb` service behavior to create `/etc/sdkwork/router/clawrouter.toml`, `/etc/sdkwork/router/clawrouter.env`, and `/etc/sdkwork/router/database.secret`, then enable but not start `clawrouter.service` until PostgreSQL is configured.
- Simplified Ubuntu/Debian installation documentation to `apt install`, protected PostgreSQL TOML/password configuration, `systemctl start clawrouter`, then health checks.
- Standardized the external runtime surface on `clawrouter`: package assets use `clawrouter-*`, the gateway executable and process are `clawrouter`, the installer/admin CLI is `clawrouterctl`, the Linux service is `clawrouter.service`, and runtime paths use `/opt/sdkwork/router`, `/etc/sdkwork/router`, `/etc/sdkwork/router/clawrouter.env`, `/var/lib/sdkwork/router`, and `/var/log/sdkwork/router`.
- Removed release package checkout dependency on Git LFS by keeping Rust `include_str!` runtime skill seed files as small curated JSON files in Git. Large ClawHub mirror snapshots remain optional Git LFS data and are not required for release builds.

## SDK And Dependency Notes

- Historical local development used sibling workspace entries for `sdkwork-appbase`, `sdkwork-core`, and `sdkwork-ui`.
- The shared repository gate was satisfied before publication: `sdkwork-appbase` was clean at `3280447`, `sdkwork-core` was committed and pushed at `339ab3e`, and `sdkwork-ui` was committed and pushed at `a4c9094`.
- Historical release notes that referenced operator-specific checkout paths are now represented through repository ids and refs only; current builds should consume dependencies through native workspace sibling paths.
- Each dependency repository reported a clean `main...origin/main` state with `HEAD...@{u}` equal to `0 0` after publication preparation.

The following local checks were run during preparation:

- `cargo fmt --all`
- `cargo test -p sdkwork-clawrouter-app-api-server --test app_session_route -- --nocapture`
- `cargo test -p sdkwork-clawrouter-router-service --test app_auth_api -- --nocapture`

- `node scripts/plan-claw-router-install-packages.mjs --check`
- `node scripts/build-claw-router-install-package.mjs --all --check --dry-run --json`
- `node scripts/build-claw-router-native-installer.mjs --all --check --dry-run --json`
- `node scripts/run-claw-router-application.test.mjs`
- `node scripts/release-preflight.mjs --dry-run --json`
- `cargo test -p sdkwork-clawrouter-router-service --test database_installer sqlite_installer_repairs`

- GitHub Actions `Release Package` run `25957200472`, covering Linux x64, Linux arm64, Windows x64, Windows arm64, macOS x64, and macOS arm64 package jobs.

The full `pnpm verify` gate was intentionally skipped after the release operator requested direct publication because it was too slow for this release attempt.

## Risks / Remaining Work

- Because full verification was skipped by instruction, CI or a later local run should cover the full Rust workspace, portal runtime suite, production artifact build, and package smoke checks before distributing binary artifacts.
- Release packaging should continue to clean build/cache outputs before producing final artifacts.
- Git LFS remains required only when refreshing the large ClawHub mirror snapshots, not when building or installing release packages.
- If a future GitHub release attempt fails after this note is committed, merge those notes into the next successful release record instead of leaving a stranded version note.
